To: Principal, Ms. Wong
From: [Your Name], Chairperson, Environmental Club

Subject: Proposal for "No Plastic Week" Initiative

I am writing to propose the implementation of a "No Plastic Week" on campus, scheduled from November 6th to 10th. This initiative is deemed essential by the Environmental Club to significantly elevate awareness regarding the pervasive issue of plastic pollution and to cultivate sustainable habits amongst the student body.

During "No Plastic Week," we envision a multifaceted approach. Initially, we will establish informative lunchtime booths that vividly illustrate the detrimental environmental impact of single-use plastics. Furthermore, we are planning a school-wide competition designed to challenge students creatively to minimize their plastic footprint; attractive prizes will be awarded to those who devise the most innovative and effective solutions. In addition, we intend to collaborate with local environmental organizations to conduct enriching workshops centered on the principles of recycling and upcycling, thus providing practical skills and knowledge.

The Environmental Club is confident that the successful execution of "No Plastic Week" will lead to a demonstrable reduction in plastic waste generated on campus and will serve as a catalyst for the adoption of eco-friendly practices in the daily lives of our students. We eagerly anticipate the opportunity to discuss this proposal in greater detail and address any inquiries you may have. Thank you for your time and thoughtful consideration.

writing.text:
To: Principal, Ms. Wong
From: [Your Name], Environmental Club Chairperson

Subject: Proposal for “No Plastic Week”

I am writing to propose a “No Plastic Week” on campus from November 6th to 10th. Our club believes this initiative is crucial to raising awareness about plastic pollution and promoting sustainable habits amongst students.

During “No Plastic Week”, we envision several activities. Firstly, we'll organise informative lunchtime booths showcasing the environmental impact of single-use plastics. Secondly, we plan a school-wide competition challenging students to reduce their plastic consumption. Prizes will be awarded for the most creative and effective solutions. We could also partner with local environmental groups to conduct workshops on recycling and upcycling.

The Environmental Club is confident that “No Plastic Week” will significantly reduce plastic waste on campus and encourage students to adopt eco-friendly practices in their daily lives. We are eager to discuss this proposal further and answer any questions you may have. Thank you for your time and consideration.

While the answers are accurate, the language used lacks the sophistication and depth of analysis required for a Level 5 grade. The language is clear and effective, but simpler.

answers.r3: The 'twofold' problem refers to the environmental issues arising from both the production and disposal stages of fast fashion. The production process consumes vast amounts of water and releases harmful chemicals, while the disposal of cheap, low-quality clothes contributes to overflowing landfills.
answers.r4: Mark Liu suggests that people treat clothes as disposable items, similar to disposable cups. He implies that clothes are often worn briefly, perhaps for a single social media post, and then discarded, highlighting a culture of excessive consumption and waste.
